decisions.reason: As a close-to-core digital module for consent and anamnesis, it fits the firm’s software base and healthcare digitization trend, so after several years the option value looks more likely to justify continued low-cost exploitation than abandonment.

The education institute is adjacent to the firm’s support and training capabilities and can deepen customer relationships, so management would likely keep it while the carrying cost remains manageable despite it being less core than software modules.

Remote screen-sharing support is useful for service delivery and likely inexpensive to maintain, so even if differentiation is limited the option is still worth keeping unless usage has clearly disappointed.

A practice analytics dashboard is strongly aligned with the firm’s direction toward connected and efficient practice management, making it a strategically attractive extension to retain and develop further.

A complete practice bundle is very close to the established offer and mainly repackages existing capabilities, so it is cheap to keep and valuable as a commercial option for different customer segments.

The job and practice listing portal is distant from the core business, likely needs separate marketplace-building efforts, and after a few years its uncertain value would no longer justify keeping this weaker option open.
